notes: An assessment tool for VCF Automation estates. The README and the sdd-workflow specifications are read by engineers deciding whether to run it and by the people acting on its findings, so precision comes before conformity to any style guide.

asd_ste100.notes: Advisory evidence under this profile, not a standard this tool claims to meet. Issue 9 is the only one installed.

rules.guidance: The product is VCF Automation. Use Aria Automation only where a historical version, a UI label, an API name, a repository name or a quoted source requires it.
rules.notes: Naming the superseded product misidentifies which release a reader is on, and the two are not interchangeable in the API surface this tool reads.

style.notes: Ranks 2 to 4, above both style guides. Kept short on purpose: a rule here is one a reviewer has to apply by hand every time, so it earns its place or goes.

spelling.directive: Project house style. Rank 4 under technical-readability, which is above both Google and ASD-STE100 Issue 9.
spelling.notes: Also the house-style spelling rule under this profile: style_policy.py generates it from this field, and only british outranks Google's American spelling.

paths.notes: Descriptive project overview and a findings reference, with procedural Install, Run and Development sections. Write those three as procedures and the rest as description.
sdd-workflow task lists. Each entry is an instruction, so the 20-word procedural sentence limit applies.
sdd-workflow specifications. Requirements and architecture decisions are description, not instruction.
